scope: Public English title and abstract versus complete Chinese translation and quicklook only; no full text or external knowledge supplementation.
method: Independent direct rereading of all three current complete Chinese translations and quicklooks against the fixed public English titles and abstracts. Current source hashes and all literal quotes checked locally; six production Node validations rerun and checked against the current six cache values.

confirmed: All source sections and outcome estimates are represented in the complete translation.
36 studies, 2 617 942 women, cohort/comparator mean ages and SDs, 16.0-year follow-up and 4.8–36.0 range retain correct units and assignments.
All-cause mortality, cardiovascular events, coronary disease and stroke PHRs and CIs remain attached to the correct outcomes.
Before-age-45 mortality excess and null estimates at or after age 45 are preserved.
The composite-outcome meta-regression is explicitly post hoc; 5-year increment, HR 0.89, CI 0.83–0.97, 37 estimates and 11 populations are preserved.
Quicklook retains association wording and the age-stratified mortality qualifier; finding quotes occur literally in this source.
The revised final conclusion now explicitly says older age is associated with progressively lower risk; association and post hoc meta-regression boundaries remain intact.

resolvedIssues.draftText: 医源性绝经年龄越大，心血管疾病发生和死亡风险越低
resolvedIssues.sourceQuote: Older age at iatrogenic menopause was associated with progressively lower risk of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality

resolvedIssues.resolution: Current draft contains the suggested qualifier and was independently reread against the fixed public abstract.

confirmed: The parent trial is randomized and a 100-patient pilot; the presented HCE analysis is explicitly post hoc.
Short-term corticosteroid therapy, prednisone, and acute heart failure remain correctly identified.
The hierarchy retains 90-day death, 90-day HF readmission, 30-day worsening HF and 30-day baseline EQ-VAS change.
Site stratification and baseline EQ-VAS adjustment remain distinct from the endpoint hierarchy.
Win ratio 1.82 and win odds 1.71, both p<0.05, 10% ties, and 26.1% overall win difference are preserved.
Little EQ-VAS effect and no substantial change in estimated win odds after adjustment are retained.
A positive pilot signal is framed as supporting further examination, without a confirmatory efficacy claim.
Quicklook finding quotes occur literally in this source and preserve the statistical and design qualifiers.
The complete translation retains intravenous routes, emergency-department presentation, recent-onset paroxysmal AF, documented CAD and absence of residual or active ischemia.
Investigator-initiated, multicenter, open-label randomization and 1:1 allocation are preserved.
Primary efficacy is within 6 hours; primary safety is the specified 6-hour composite, including bradycardia below 50 bpm; 24-hour ECG monitoring remains distinct.
Eighty-seven randomized patients, 42 flecainide and 45 amiodarone, remain correctly assigned; Chinese words preserve the source spelled-out total.
Six-hour conversion 85.7% versus 40.0%, median 20 versus 244 minutes, admission 14.3% versus 60.0%, and associated P<0.001 values remain correctly assigned.
No ventricular proarrhythmic events within 24 hours and no deaths through 30 days are preserved with their separate windows.
The conclusion and quicklook limits explicitly retain the hypothesis-generating interpretation of the short-term no-serious-ventricular-proarrhythmia finding.
No claim of established long-term safety or a clinical recommendation is added; finding quotes occur literally in this source.
The revised standalone one-line summary now retains absence of residual or active ischemia, matching the selected population.

limitations: This is a second model review, not human or medical final review. No fabricated provider usage or exact actual model identity is asserted.
writeScope: Only this review JSON updated; current drafts, sources, cache and ledger unchanged by reviewer.
sourcePolicy: Only the fixed current 24-paper sources snapshot is used; the two historical source-repair identities are absent from this snapshot and were not supplemented or reused in this review. Acceptance is tied to the recorded source hashes and file hashes.
